title: Stable Subarrays With Equal Boundary and Interior Sum
summary: Given an integer array, count the subarrays where the first and last elements are each the sum of the elements between them, and the subarray length is at least 3.
statement: Given an integer array, count the subarrays where the first and last elements are each the sum of the elements between them, and the subarray length is at least 3.
constraints: capacity contains three to 100,000 signed integers.
A stable subarray has length at least three.
Its first and last values are equal to each other and to the sum of all strict interior values.
hints: For endpoints l and r, stability is equivalent to equal boundary values and prefix[r]=capacity[l]+prefix[l+1].
As r advances, add l=r-2 to a map keyed by exactly those two required left-side quantities.
Query the map with (capacity[r], prefix[r]) and add its frequency.
Every eligible left endpoint enters before its matching rights and the key equality is algebraically identical to both stability conditions.
editorial: Every eligible left endpoint enters before its matching rights and the key equality is algebraically identical to both stability conditions.

tests.explanation: The whole array and the middle [3,3,3] are stable, giving two.
No equal-boundary subarray also matches its interior sum.
